content.comment_body: I'm working with an older circuit and want to be able to adjust the timer remotely. I attempted this using [product_name] Web Editor, but it's not functioning as expected. The main issue is transferring analog timer data from the webpage to the schematic. I've tried several configurations, such as using an analog input to send timer data, which works in simulation mode but fails with [product_name] Web Editor because the input field isn't writable. On the actual webpage, you cannot change the value since inputs aren’t editable. The only writable options in [product_name] Web Editor are outputs or markers, and while changing those reflects on the circuit, the timer parameter won’t accept the new value. I use an analog amplifier between the input and the timer because direct analog inputs aren't accepted by timer fields. I've also experimented with other methods like VM parameter transfers, flags, and network input/outputs, but nothing resolves the problem. Digital inputs behave similarly; I tried adding a pushbutton on the webpage, but only physical inputs are recognized. It’s possible the AX parameter of the analog amplifier, described as an input while AQ is the output, is contributing to the confusion. The output should be connectable to the timer parameter input, but the documentation seems inconsistent. Any ideas on how to address this? Please refer to the Word attachment for circuit diagrams and screenshots of the [product_name] Web Editor setup. Thank you! [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no], [product_name] Web Editor [version_no], [product_name] [article_no], Firmware [version_no], hardware [version_no]

First, it's not possible to write values to physical analog inputs remotely; only the hardware can do that. However, you can use network analog inputs whose addresses are in the VM memory. Second, parameter-VM-mapping with a scaled time feature in [product_name] Web Editor allows you to write timer parameters directly.
I've prepared an example for you.
Thank you! Your suggestion was extremely helpful. I tried entering values for the delay block directly via VM and it works perfectly.
Does this mean your problem is resolved now?

analysis.insight_summary: Participants highlighted the challenge of remotely updating timer settings in older [company_name] circuits through the web editor. The inability to directly write analog values to timer parameters via the web interface stems from design limitations, as physical analog inputs cannot be modified remotely. Alternative solutions like using network analog inputs and parameter-VM-mapping were shared and proven effective. The discussion also pointed out that the documentation or user interface may lack clarity regarding remote parameter management options and restrictions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to control timer parameters remotely through the web interface, specifically to adjust analog values on timer blocks for more flexible and online control of circuit behavior.
